blogs.title: The 'Metabolic Mimic': Why Young-Onset Diabetes Isn't Always Type 1 or Type 2
blogs.description: This post explores the diagnostic pitfalls of Maturity-Onset Diabetes of the Young (MODY). We will analyze why the patient's presentation—including weight loss, polyuria, and metabolic syndrome markers—mimicked classic Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes, leading to an initial misdiagnosis. The discussion will focus on the 'grey zone' in young-onset diabetes where traditional clinical heuristics (BMI, autoantibodies, ketone status) fail to distinguish monogenic causes from common phenotypes.

blogs.title: Beyond Autoantibodies: Leveraging Glucagon Stimulation Tests and Family History for MODY Suspicion
blogs.description: Focusing on the pre-genetic workup, this article breaks down how to identify candidates for molecular testing when standard markers are ambiguous. We will dissect the utility of the glucagon stimulation test (C-peptide dynamics) combined with a rigorous three-generation pedigree analysis. The post will argue that a strong family history of early-onset diabetes paired with negative autoantibodies should trigger a MODY screen regardless of BMI or metabolic syndrome features.

blogs.title: Genetic Nuances: Interpreting Novel Variants and the Role of AlphaMissense in Precision Medicine
blogs.description: This technical deep dive focuses on the specific case finding: a novel *HNF1A* variant (p.N270S) absent from ClinVar. We will walk through the application of ACMG guidelines for variant interpretation, explaining how bioinformatic tools like AlphaMissense scores and functional domain mapping (DNA-binding vs. transactivation domains) allow clinicians to classify 'Variants of Uncertain Significance' as Pathogenic/Likely Pathogenic based on structural biology and segregation data.

blogs.title: From Insulin to GLP-1: Re-evaluating Pharmacotherapy Algorithms in HNF1A-MODY
blogs.description: While sulfonylureas remain the historical gold standard for HNF1A-MODY, this post challenges the immediate initiation of insulin in newly diagnosed patients with moderate beta-cell preservation. We will review evidence supporting GLP-1 receptor agonists (like dulaglutide) as a potent alternative that preserves beta-cell mass while minimizing hypoglycemia risk. The discussion includes a stepwise algorithm for de-escalating insulin once genetic confirmation is achieved.

blogs.title: The SGLT2 Trap: Why Renal Threshold Changes in HNF1A-MODY Contraindicate Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter Inhibitors
blogs.description: A safety-focused educational piece detailing the unique pathophysiology of HNF1A-MODY regarding renal glucose handling. Unlike typical Type 2 diabetes, *HNF1A* mutations cause a profound reduction in SGLT2 expression and renal glucose threshold. This post explains why prescribing SGLT2 inhibitors in these patients can precipitate severe dehydration, euglycemic DKA, or vascular collapse, emphasizing the need to avoid this drug class entirely in confirmed HNF1A-MODY cases.
